title: The Freak Book
description: A V3-first Book skeleton for the FREAK Academy connector. It introduces implemented basics only and cross-links each chapter to lessons and reference entries owned by this repository.

parts.title: Part I: Getting Started
parts.summary: The first path through FREAK: files, output, and the smallest useful program.

chapters.title: Hello, FREAK
chapters.summary: Start with a `.fk` file and the `say` statement, then connect the terminal lesson to the browser Academy flow.

sections.title: The smallest useful program
sections.body: A FREAK program can start as a single statement. The first Academy release uses the V3 compiler path, so this chapter teaches only syntax that the current terminal and browser workers can evaluate.

sections.title: What `say` does
sections.body: `say` evaluates one expression and writes the rendered value followed by a newline. In the current Academy subset, exact output is the simplest reliable check shared by terminal and browser exercises.

chapters.title: Words and Output
chapters.summary: Use double-quoted `word` literals as the first visible values in a program.

sections.title: Word values
sections.body: A `word` literal is text between double quotes. Printing words first keeps the beginner path focused on observable behavior before introducing declarations and types.

parts.title: Part II: Core Language
parts.summary: The implemented V3 Academy subset: values, expressions, control flow, loops, and tasks.

chapters.title: Variables and Types
chapters.summary: `pilot` gives a value a local name. Type annotations make intent explicit when a lesson needs that clarity.

sections.title: Declare a value
sections.body: Use `pilot` for a local binding. The initializer runs once, and later expressions can use the name.

sections.title: Starter types
sections.body: The first Academy pass uses `int` and `word` because they are enough to explain declarations, output, arithmetic, and basic control flow without reaching into V4-only language services.

chapters.title: Expressions and Control Flow
chapters.summary: Combine values with operators, branch with `if` and `else`, and repeat a block with the counted loop form.

sections.title: Combine values
sections.body: Expressions produce values. Operators such as `+` and `*` make new values from smaller expressions.

examples.title: Calculate before printing
examples.source:
pilot width = 8
pilot height = 4
say width * height

sections.title: Choose and repeat
sections.body: The current Academy lessons keep control flow direct: use a boolean comparison for `if`, provide an `else` branch, and use `repeat N times` when the number of iterations is known.

chapters.title: Tasks
chapters.summary: A `task` names a reusable unit of work with parameters and a return value.

sections.title: Name work
sections.body: Tasks make repeated logic explicit. In the V3 Academy subset, a task can take typed parameters, return a value, and be called from a later expression.
